lead.title: Founder | Helping B2B revenue teams forecast from buyer evidence

insights.summary: Founder explicitly skeptical of AI lead-gen overpromise and committed to buyer evidence over opinion. Vantera's accuracy guarantee, review-first workflow, and hard weekly send ceilings align directly with their revenue philosophy. Strong fit for a conversation on how to scale qualified pipeline without sacrificing control.
triggers: Recent articulation of concern for AI accuracy in lead generation
Focus on deal truth and forecast confidence suggests active pipeline challenges
insights.aha_moment: Running a 2-week pilot where Vantera's AI scores prospects and you approve every message, proving accuracy on your own pipeline before scaling.
motivations: Build trusted pipeline with verifiable buyer signals
Replace guesswork with data-driven revenue decisions
Maintain control and approval over outreach at scale
pain_points: Skepticism of AI lead-gen promises and false positives
Need for buyer evidence over opinion-driven pipeline decisions
insights.value_angle: Vantera's 98% accuracy scoring and review-first send model give your sales outreach the rigor and control your own revenue philosophy demands — no black-box sends, every message approved before it goe
insights.prospect_offering: Founder building solutions for B2B revenue teams to replace pipeline opinion with buyer evidence and forecast confidence.

context.cta: a short walkthrough of how Vantera books qualified meetings
context.valueProp: Vantera finds in-market prospects on LinkedIn, drafts personal messages, and books qualified meetings while the founder approves every send

turns.text: Your framing around replacing pipeline opinion with buyer evidence is sharp. That tension between gut-feel forecasting and actual deal truth is underrated.

Appreciate the connect, Trevor. You've written about AI accuracy in lead-gen being a real problem, and I'm curious how you currently vet whether a prospect is actually in-market before outreach goes out.
That's honest. What do you use to decide who to reach out to in the first place?

notes: 'I dont.' was classified not_interested and suppressed in production; it is a terse answer. He then asked 'Why do you ask?' twice and nobody could answer (suppressed). A question must be answered: wait is vetoed.
